newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent thin, rangebound but eyes Iraq exports.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent thin, rangebound but eyes Iraq exports.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were marginally firmer on Thursday in what brokers said was a lull following the expiry of the August contract yesterdat.
Players were also taking stock of news of a potentially higher rate of exports from Iraq in August.
September Brent crude was at $18.32 a barrel at 0935 GMT, just two cents a barrel up from Wednesday's close, while August gas oil was 25 cents a tonne up at $164.00.
"It has quietened down after the expiry yesterday," one broker said, adding that he though that the market would likely be rangebound between $18.25 and $18.45.

The U.N. confirmed late on Wednesday a Reuters report that Iraq will not be allowed to carry more than five percent of its $1 billion allowance into the second 90-day tranche of a current six-month, $2 billion oil-for-food sales deal, which came into effect on June 8.

Because of delays in lifting Iraqi crude so far this means the $1 billion worth of oil will have to be squeezed into a much shorter time period, which could mean exports of over 1.5 million barrels per day in August/early September.

"The questions are whether Iraq currently has the ability to move this much oil - debateable; whether or not buyers will be willing to offload this much - difficult," said brokers GNI in a daily report.
"The Iraq news is a bearish development if Baghdad does attempt to maximise output."

Technical analysts said they saw $18.45-$18.50 as a particularly strong area of resistance - corresponding to a falling trendline on the weekly continuation chart, as well as to triple tops formed on the September contract chart and the continuation chart.

"Crude markets are hovering up around tough range resistance but do not seem to have the strength to break through as yet - perhaps the worry of an imminent supply surge from Iraq is keeping prices within the range," said Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives.
